title: Row of a matrix product difference
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A$, $B$, and $C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over the field with two elements, and let $i$ be a row index. The row of the matrix product difference at index $i$ is the function on column indices $j$ whose value is the matrix product difference of $A$, $B$, and $C'$ at $(i,j)$.
hypotheses_covered: $A,B,C'$ are matrices indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$ over the field with two elements
caveat: The supplied snippet does not include the definition of the matrix product difference, so its precise formula cannot be stated from the given ground truth.
